documents.title: Educational Technology - Current Students (Generative AI Tools)
documents.summary: A section of the school's educational technology page that describes generative AI tools available to students (Copilot, ChatGPT, Grammarly, a locally hosted Llama chat, Qualified Health AI). It mostly warns about data and IP exposure and which licenses are FERPA and HIPAA compliant, and says little about academic use.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule on what AI may be used for in coursework or on grading, so it is not a ban. It lists tools students may use and says to check the 'GPT Comparison Matrix before using GPTs for coursework and research', so students may use AI with data-protection conditions: permit.

documents.unit: McGovern Medical School (Center for Humanities and Ethics)
documents.title: Policy on AI Generative Tools
documents.summary: The McGovern Center's policy for its programs lets students consult AI tools in limited listed situations, requires citation, bans AI-generated reflective writing and AI-generated references, and says detection software will be used. It leaves other decisions to faculty and departments and can be revised.
documents.stance_why: The policy says 'Students may consult AI generative tools in limited situations' and lists narrow uses (clarifying terms, summarizing supplementary text, editing), with permission advised for artwork or writing and a ban on AI reflections: AI is allowed only for narrow listed uses, which is restrict.

units.why: The Background defines ChatGPT and other GPT language models ('ChatGPT is but one example of a GPT'), setting what tools the policy covers, so P61 informs.
units.anchor: ChatGPT is but one example of a GPT
units.frag_start: ChatGPT is but one example
units.frag_end: Similar AI tools use one of these language models.

units.why: It says 'AI tools can be used in responsible ways' and that people are 'figuring out how to incorporate these tools to support teaching and learning and explore their benefits', a statement of benefit and openness (informs), P87 rather than a rule.
units.anchor: AI tools can be used in responsible ways
units.frag_start: Concerns over plagiarism, ethics, and academic
units.frag_end: which must be understood when using them.
units.fit_note: Also acknowledges plagiarism and ethics concerns alongside the benefits.

units.why: The text warns 'artificial hallucination is possible', including 'citations to non-existent references'; users 'should be aware of their limitations', which is about AI output being wrong (P31).

units.policy: Users should be aware that AI tools have limitations, including hallucination such as citations to non-existent references.
